In his letter, CM Revanth said the verification process had placed particular stress on voters classified as “permanently shifted”. He cautioned that ordinary mobility, temporary absence and relocation for work or marriage should not become grounds for disenfranchisement. According to the data furnished by the EC, Telangana had 3.38 crore electors as on June 10. Of these, 73.39 lakh entries, or 21.7%, have been classified under the Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD) categories. Of the 2.65 crore enumeration forms digitised so far, 60.50 lakh have been flagged for anomalies and 32.36 lakh for lack of a link to the previous electoral roll. items.title: Not a good sign when bar council does not earn respect of its members: Supreme Court Justice BV Nagarathna
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice BV Nagarathna on Saturday that bar councils must introspect on their role in upholding professional ethics, morality and competence. "The Bar Councils, whether the Central or the States, must introspect their role and importance in upholding professional ethics, morality and professional competence. When a Bar Council does not earn the respect of its members, it is not a good sign for the legal profession," she said. Justice Nagarathna made these observations while delivering an address at the 13th convocation of National Law University, Delhi on August 29, 2026. Also present were Delhi High Court Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, who is Chancellor of the University, judges of the Delhi High Court and Vice-Chancellor Prof GS Bajpai. Her remarks come weeks after a controversy involving Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, who had directed state bar councils not to enrol the graduating 2026 batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad as advocates after they objected to the invitation of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant for their own convocation. items.title: Take appointment of arbitrators away from parties, institutionalise process: Shashank Garg
items.summary: Senior Advocate Shashank Garg on Thursday called for the appointment of arbitrators to be taken away from parties and entrusted to courts or arbitral institutions. Garg said institutional appointments would ensure that arbitrators did not owe their positions to parties or law firms. He acknowledged that the proposal would curtail party autonomy and require further deliberation. “ Take party autonomy away from the appointment process. Let arbitrators be appointed either by the court or by institutions so that arbitrators do not have any masters, so to say. They have no allegiance to firms and no interest arising from who appointed them. The State’s faith in arbitration can then probably be restored, ” he said. “ Half of our problems will go if the appointment of arbitrators is taken away from the parties and is done in an institutional manner. Of course, it is not something that we can move towards right away. It would require a lot more thought and debate. But if we are able to bring this significant change, it will impact us in a very positive way ,” Garg added. The MOU was signed on 28 August at GCAI’s “India-Singapore Legal Bridge: Enabling Growth, Investment and Effective Dispute Resolution in a Changing Global Economy” event, held on the sidelines of Singapore Convention Week. The event brought together legal and business leaders to discuss the India-Singapore-ASEAN investment landscape and the role of the legal profession in supporting cross-border growth. The event was attended by Supreme Court Justice Manmohan , Attorney General for India R Venkataramani , Deputy High Commissioner of India in Singapore Sudhi Chowdhary and Drew & Napier Chairman Jimmy Yim , among others. The partnership aims to focus on knowledge exchange, professional development and greater cross-border engagement between in-house counsel in the two jurisdictions.
